polls.text: MCR's question on use of a wiki for existing draft:

(1) YES: I like the wiki (2) No: I preferred to write and publish an normativeRFC, even if it delays other documents (3) No Opinion: I prefer a WIP I-D that will be informatively referenced, and eventually published

chat.author: Henk Birkholz
chat.text: Hi all!

chat.author: Henk Birkholz
chat.text: Happy :rat::rat::rat: day

chat.author: Mark Novak
chat.text: TACRA draft link: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-novak-rats-tacra/

chat.author: Michael Richardson
chat.text: morning.

chat.author: Kathleen Moriarty
chat.text: Good morning! Sorry for being a few minutes late, I was transitioning from last meeting.

chat.author: Nathanael Ritz
chat.text: Morning!

chat.author: Tom Sato
chat.text: confirming Sardars "why email I sent" which I will also cover a bit.

chat.author: Michael Richardson
chat.text: Chairs, 30min ago, the multi-verifier/composite verifier design team discussed the move of the taxonomy to a wiki.  We'd like to poll the WG, if there is time, on whether this was the right move.

chat.author: Kathleen Moriarty
chat.text: Michael, noted. I will add myself to the queue as chair.

chat.author: Ned Smith
chat.text: We have some open mic time at the end of the meeting. Can you bring it up then?

chat.author: Kathleen Moriarty
chat.text: Ned - I'll speak on this work (current draft under review) again as chair.

chat.author: Ned Smith
chat.text: :blush:

chat.author: Michael Richardson
chat.text: This is not the security considerations template I asked for at 124.

chat.author: Kathleen Moriarty
chat.text: And it doesn't follow the guidance I provided.

chat.author: Michael Richardson
chat.text:
Ned Smith said:

We have some open mic time at the end of the meeting. Can you bring it up then?

I suggest a poll: (1) I like the wiki (2) I preferred to write and publish an normativeRFC, even if it delays other documents (3) I prefer a WIP I-D that will be informatively referenced, and eventually published (4) wait? What happened?

chat.author: Yogesh Deshpande
chat.text: @ Michael in that case of poll, I would request you share the link of Wiki and Draft Version 04

chat.author: Kathleen Moriarty
chat.text: Thanks, Michael. I can draft the poll when we gat closer to the open mic time.

chat.author: Michael Richardson
chat.text: Wiki: https://wiki.ietf.org/group/rats/atomic-composites  I-D: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-richardson-rats-composite-attesters/

chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text:
Michael Richardson said:

This is not the security considerations template I asked for at 124.

We believe guidance on security considerations is actually more helpful than just template.

chat.author: Songbo Bu
chat.text: I think security guidelines is something what we need most in RATS.

chat.author: Kathleen Moriarty
chat.text: Songbo, Yes, please watch back the end of the IETF123 session. This is not disputed, but how they are provided is the point that was not met.

chat.author: Giridhar Mandyam
chat.text: Re: CCA CoRIM, sorry I did not review this properly yet.  Device assignment is part of realm extensions, isn't it?  So what is the provenance of DA-related measurements?

chat.author: Kathleen Moriarty
chat.text: Updates belong in a draft and they must be factually written without opinions. Then a wiki can be used to provide guidance for existing drafts.

chat.author: Songbo Bu
chat.text: When there are critical-severity attacks, it means something needs to be corrected.

chat.author: Kathleen Moriarty
chat.text: @Songbo That's accomplished with errata or updates drafts.

chat.author: Kathleen Moriarty
chat.text: We need to follow established norms and practices for the IETF so that the wider community understands where to look for guidance.

chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text:
Kathleen Moriarty said:

Updates belong in a draft and they must be factually written without opinions. Then a wiki can be used to provide guidance for existing drafts.

We will remove the current drafts until next draft version and focus only on guidance.

chat.author: Kathleen Moriarty
chat.text: Guidance is in a wiki. Updates to published RFCs are in a draft. Updates to drafts are on the list and in discussions.

chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text: I don't think wiki is very accessible.

chat.author: Carl Wallace
chat.text: Section 1.6 lists three items in scope. Are you cutting that down to one item? That will make for a much much shorter draft.

chat.author: Yogesh Deshpande
chat.text: The earlier version with expanded draft was

chat.author: Yogesh Deshpande
chat.text: https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-richardson-rats-composite-attesters-04.html

chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text:
Carl Wallace said:

Section 1.6 lists three items in scope. Are you cutting that down to one item? That will make for a much much shorter draft.

Correct. That's what we had in our last slide:


General security baseline that other drafts can simply point to, or guidelines or template that other drafts can use

chat.author: Kathleen Moriarty
chat.text: Usama, that is what will be accepted. The guidance will be applied in drafts and is enforced in the WG publication process. This is standard practice for the IETF and has been for decades.

chat.author: Camilo Posada
chat.text: I want to speak to the problem this draft raises. Attestation security considerations are genuinely under-served, RFC 9334 gives us the architecture, but the concrete 'what can go wrong, and how do you fail closed' guidance is thin, and real deployments feel that gap. So I think the problem is real and worth this group's attention, and I'd encourage the working group to engage with the work.

chat.author: Ned Smith
chat.text: KIA seems a little like Linux IMA.

chat.author: Hannes Tschofenig
chat.text: Would be interesting to see whether there is a comparison with the Linux IMA and KIA available

chat.author: Giridhar Mandyam
chat.text: Re: key attestation.  "The Evidence names no key, so nothing ties K_bad_private to the TEE."  The pubkey can be included in the challenge data.  What is the reason(s) that this is insufficient?

chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text:
Kathleen Moriarty said:

Usama, that is what will be accepted. The guidance will be applied in drafts and is enforced in the WG publication process. This is standard practice for the IETF and has been for decades.

I am not aware of any such standard practice. Could chairs please provide a normative reference emphasizing this? Guidance could be in wiki, but nothing seems to preclude it to be in draft of its own.

chat.author: Giridhar Mandyam
chat.text: Continued from above:  If only TEE can provide a field in the challenge data then that would differentiate a TEE-bound keypair from a 'bad' kepypair.

chat.author: Kathleen Moriarty
chat.text: Usama, references have been provided. See how security guidance is covered for YANG and SNMP before that. Please also see how errata and RFC Updates are used. This is established practice.

chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text: The point is wiki is much less accessible than draft and given the CVEs of 9.1 and upto 10.0, there is a need for guidance to implementers and draft.

chat.author: Tom Sato
chat.text: Ned, Hannes: IMA measures software identity (hashes of loaded binaries, chained into a PCR); KIA signs governance decisions (mandates, escalations, revocations), chained via the GEC's own keypair rather than a PCR extend. Different layer, same shape — happy to write up a fuller comparison and post it to the Rats wg ml

chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text:
Kathleen Moriarty said:

Usama, references have been provided. See how security guidance is covered for YANG and SNMP before that. Please also see how errata and RFC Updates are used. This is established practice.

That's what YANG and SNMP end up doing. I requested a normative reference which says guidance cannot be a draft.

chat.author: Kathleen Moriarty
chat.text: Usama, please follow established norms.

chat.author: Ned Smith
chat.text: Different layer, same shape — happy to write up a fuller comparison and post it to the Rats wg ml:grinning:

chat.author: Giridhar Mandyam
chat.text: @kathleen, what is to prevent Usama from taking his draft outside of RATS and working directly with the RFC editor?  It could allow us to get past the discussion of this draft in the RATS WG.

chat.author: Kathleen Moriarty
chat.text:
Giri, He could try working with the ISE, but the ISE checks with the WG for conflicts. This work should happen in the WG, but should follow norms. We are not trying to prevent his work, but rather have it work within the established set of norms. 
The ISE would also object to section 1.4 and any other sections that have similar opinions and would not accept it as a starting point.

chat.author: Kathleen Moriarty
chat.text: ISE = Independent Stream Editor

chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text: Several authors have genuinely benefited from the draft. Wiki is not accessible. I am yet to see the normative reference. When there are CVEs of the level of 9.1 and up to 10.0, I think there is need of active guidance from the WG and not passively in wiki. That's the only point.

chat.author: Carl Wallace
chat.text: You profess to have anticipated the complaints so you know what the issues are and have indicated plans to tighten the scope so let us see what the next draft brings.

chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text:
Carl, I am not sure what that means. We will release a new update scoping it to just the following and see what people say: 


General security baseline that other drafts can simply point to, or guidelines or template that other drafts can use

chat.author: Carl Wallace
chat.text: Right. So we see what comes and resume discussion then.

chat.author: Kathleen Moriarty
chat.text: Usama, please follow the provided guidance. No has said the work is not useful, we are looking for you to follow established norms as a prerequisite to accepting the work. The same guidance has been provided 5 times now and will not change. I'd like to see you adapt how you present the work. I will respond again when we see the updated formats, but will need to drop the conversation until then as the answers will remain in accordance with IETF established norms even if they do not match your preferences.

chat.author: Kathleen Moriarty
chat.text: Guidance for drafts - wiki; Updates draft for published RFCs with factual statements and information on why the change, plus the Updates text; Drafts can receive comments on the list or following the git process.

chat.author: Ned Smith
chat.text: Does support of future credentials extend to W3C verifiable credentials / DIDs and IETF SPICE related work?

chat.author: Nathanael Ritz
chat.text: I would imagine so

chat.author: Michael Richardson
chat.text: Yeah, coordination with LAMPS important.  Note LAMPS is enthusiastic about RFC7030bis, but that hasn't started yet.  Extending 7030/EST is not easy today.

chat.author: Michael Richardson
chat.text: I'm up for bikeshedding replacement for RATS "RP"  term :-)

chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text: which draft is the poll?

chat.author: Michael Richardson
chat.text: The three choices are okay if we can't do anything else :-)

chat.author: Yogesh Deshpande
chat.text: https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-richardson-rats-composite-attesters-04.html

chat.author: Yogesh Deshpande
chat.text: https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-richardson-rats-composite-attesters-05.html

chat.author: Nathanael Ritz
chat.text: "Le Grand Verificateur" - someone was having fun

chat.author: Michael Richardson
chat.text:
Nathanael Ritz said:

"Le Grand Verificateur" - someone was having fun

It wasn't me.  I love whimsy, but it was Jun. Bless him.

chat.author: Michael Richardson
chat.text: This Work would, I think, always be In Progress.

chat.author: Michael Richardson
chat.text: WIKI.ietf.org is editable by anyone with a DT account, but also via github PR, and we can review.

chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text: There are living drafts which are never published. Nobody reads wiki.

chat.author: Muhammad Usama Sardar
chat.text: This is useful work.

chat.author: Ned Smith
chat.text: Can a github / wiki be used as an informational reference in an RFC

chat.author: Michael Richardson
chat.text:
Muhammad Usama Sardar said:

There are living drafts which are never published. Nobody reads wiki.

Nobody outside of the WG reads I-D which are never published.   Documents that use the visual language would reference the wiki, same as we reference wikipedia

chat.author: Michael Richardson
chat.text:
Ned Smith said:

Can a github / wiki be used as an informational reference in an RFC

Of course.  We regularly reference wikipedia; I think I have yet to have an RFC that does not reference wikipedia at least once.

chat.author: Henk Birkholz
chat.text: Thank you all!
